numerical_failure.observed_behavior: np.histogram returns zero-width bin edges (identical consecutive edges, e.g. all edges equal to 1.0) with nonzero counts when many bins are requested over a value range close to floating-point precision, e.g. a = np.array([1, 1+2e-16] * 10) with bins=10 gives counts [0, 10, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 10] and bin edges all 1.0 (np.diff gives 0 except one 2.22044605e-16).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Instead of returning bins with zero width, histogram should raise a ValueError when the calculated bins do not all have a finite size (message: 'Too many bins for data range. Cannot create {n_equal_bins} finite-sized bins.').
trigger_conditions: many bins requested in a small value region close to numeric precision
computed bin edges are not strictly increasing (consecutive edges equal, zero bin width)
data values differ only by tiny amounts such as 2e-16 relative to 1

input_output_examples.expected_output: ValueError raised: 'Too many bins for data range. Cannot create 10 finite-sized bins.'
